functional_requirements.title: Capture the already-computed 'git worktree prune' set instead of discarding it
functional_requirements.description: lib/worktree-reaper/orphan-sweep.js (~lines 225-228) already runs `git worktree prune` best-effort and discards its output. That command's dry-run output names exactly the class this SD needs to detect: a REGISTERED worktree entry whose gitdir target no longer exists (measured live 2026-09-07: 'worktrees/SD-LEO-DOC-FOUNDATION-AUDIT-LENS-001: gitdir file points to non-existent location', 29 registered vs 36 on-disk dirs). Capture and parse this output into a distinct bucket at the sweep's existing call site -- do NOT modify lib/worktree-quota.js's classifyOrphanDirs predicate itself, which is reached on every `git worktree add` via emitOrphanWarningIfAny and must stay zero-extra-I/O (validation-agent finding, evidence 69a19709). Keep the new bucket SEPARATE from reapableDirs/orphan classification so the existing orphan gauge is not distorted.
acceptance_criteria: A pure-function test constructs a fixture matching real `git worktree prune --dry-run -v` output (a registered entry with a missing gitdir target) and asserts it lands in the new distinct bucket
The SAME fixture, run through the unmodified classifyOrphanDirs predicate, is confirmed to NOT appear there (proving the new bucket is additive, not a duplicate of existing classification)
No new git subprocess call is added to the hot `git worktree add` / emitOrphanWarningIfAny path -- the capture happens only at orphan-sweep.js's existing prune call site

functional_requirements.title: Route the new prune-set bucket through the existing durable audit sink
functional_requirements.description: Route entries from FR-0's new bucket through lib/worktree-reaper/audit-sink.js's writeAuditSink(supabase, records, {runId, logger}) into the audit_log table, mirroring the existing call convention at scripts/worktree-reaper.mjs:1751/:1955. Use a distinct event_type/reason value (never overload the existing 'worktree_reaper_classification' or 'worktree_orphan_sweep' values) so a reader can tell this class apart from ordinary orphan/reclaim rows.
acceptance_criteria: After a sweep run against a fixture containing a prune-set entry, a row is READ BACK from audit_log with the new distinct event_type/reason -- never just 'writeAuditSink returned ok' (validation-agent hazard: audit_log_severity_check silently rejects an out-of-enum severity and writeAuditSink never throws on that rejection)
The severity value used maps to one of audit_log_severity_check's allowed values ({info, warning, error, critical}) -- verified by a live insert+readback, not assumed

functional_requirements.title: Give the ship-path worktree.husk_detected event a durable consumer
functional_requirements.description: scripts/modules/shipping/post-merge-worktree-cleanup.js:393-400 emits worktree.husk_detected (this repo's OWN definition of husk: git-deregistered, directory survives -- confirmed identical in lib/worktree-reaper/close-husk.js:4 and lib/worktree-manager.js:1867-1870) via console.warn with ZERO consumers, on the /ship path specifically (cleanupWorktreeByPath, line 315). This is a DIFFERENT residue class from FR-0/FR-1's prune-set. Note: LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL's own cleanupWorktree() path already gets remediation via closeHusk (lead-final-approval/index.js:1168) but still no durable record -- this FR targets the SHIP path specifically, which gets neither today. Route this event through the same writeAuditSink mechanism as FR-1, using its own distinct event_type/reason so it is never conflated with the prune-set class.
acceptance_criteria: A simulated husk-detected event on the ship path (repo's real husk definition: deregistered, directory survives) produces a readable row in audit_log
The event_type/reason used is distinct from FR-1's prune-set event_type, so the two residue classes remain distinguishable in the durable record

functional_requirements.title: Terminology precision: never call the new (FR-0/FR-1) class a 'husk'
functional_requirements.description: This repo's own code consistently defines 'husk' as git-deregistered-but-directory-survives (close-husk.js:4, worktree-manager.js:1867-1870, post-merge-worktree-cleanup.js:381-386) -- the class classifyOrphanDirs ALREADY detects. The class this SD adds detection for (FR-0) is the OPPOSITE: registered-in-git but gitdir-target-missing (the `git worktree prune` set). Naming FR-0's class 'husk' would make any test built against the repo's real husk shape pass vacuously against unmodified code (validation-agent finding, HIGH severity). All code, comments, event_type/reason strings, and tests for FR-0/FR-1 must use 'registered entry with a missing gitdir target' / 'prune-set' terminology, never 'husk'.
acceptance_criteria: No new identifier, event_type value, or code comment introduced by FR-0/FR-1 uses the word 'husk'
A code reviewer (or the retrospective) can confirm the two residue classes (prune-set vs. this repo's husk) are never conflated in naming, tests, or the durable record's event_type values

functional_requirements.title: Unit fixtures for both residue classes, in the process file(s) actually changed
functional_requirements.description: Add unit fixtures covering: (a) FR-0's prune-set capture and bucket classification (using the real prune-set fixture shape, per FR-3), (b) FR-1's audit_log routing for a prune-set entry with a live-shape readback assertion, (c) FR-2's audit_log routing for a ship-path husk_detected event with a live-shape readback assertion, and (d) a negative fixture proving a HEALTHY registered worktree (gitdir target exists) is classified into NEITHER new bucket.
acceptance_criteria: All 4 fixture classes above exist and pass
Full existing worktree-reaper/worktree-quota test suites still pass with zero regressions

technical_requirements.requirement: FR-0's capture must not add any new git subprocess invocation -- it consumes orphan-sweep.js's EXISTING `git worktree prune` call output only
technical_requirements.rationale: orphan-sweep.js already pays this cost and discards the result; adding a second independent prune call would double the I/O for no benefit

technical_requirements.requirement: FR-1/FR-2 both write through lib/worktree-reaper/audit-sink.js's writeAuditSink -- never a hand-rolled supabase.from('audit_log').insert() call
technical_requirements.rationale: writeAuditSink is the single canonical writer for this family (used at worktree-reaper.mjs:1751/:1955); a second hand-rolled writer would drift from its severity-mapping and buildAuditRows conventions

technical_requirements.requirement: Acceptance tests for FR-1/FR-2 must assert on a value READ BACK from audit_log, never on writeAuditSink's return value alone
technical_requirements.rationale: audit_log_severity_check silently rejects an out-of-enum severity and writeAuditSink does not throw on that rejection (validation-agent finding) -- a return-value-only assertion would pass even if the row never landed

test_scenarios.scenario: Prune-set fixture is captured and bucketed (FR-0)
test_scenarios.steps: Construct a fixture matching real `git worktree prune --dry-run -v` output for a registered-but-missing-gitdir entry; assert it lands in the new distinct bucket and is absent from classifyOrphanDirs's existing orphan set
Run the sweep against the FR-0 fixture; read back audit_log and assert a row exists with the new distinct event_type/reason and an in-enum severity

exploration_summary: VALIDATION and Explore sub-agents (LEAD phase, this session) corrected the RCA's own terminology: this repo's code defines 'husk' as git-deregistered-but-directory-survives (the class classifyOrphanDirs already detects), the OPPOSITE of the 'registered but gitdir-target-missing' class the RCA actually measured and wants surfaced. The validation-agent also found that lib/worktree-reaper/orphan-sweep.js already runs `git worktree prune` and discards its output -- the exact information FR-0 needs is already computed, making capture-and-route far cheaper and lower-risk than modifying classifyOrphanDirs's hot-path predicate. Confirmed the durable sink (writeAuditSink -> audit_log) is live (rows observed landing 2026-09-07T05:11:04Z) and flagged that audit_log_severity_check silently rejects out-of-enum severities without writeAuditSink throwing, so acceptance criteria are written against a live readback, never a return-value check. Confirmed no sibling SD (A-G under the same parent) or in-flight PR overlaps this scope; separately signaled to the coordinator that fix shape 2 (cadence-schedule restoration) is UNSOURCED and needs its own ticket.
